correctness.rationale: Exact change to consensus/disagreement coordinates makes the post-broadcast error the leading component of a product of explicit 2 by 2 matrices. Direct multiplication yields the 3- and 4-broadcast formulas. The first is minimized by convex balancing. For four broadcasts, strict positivity forces balanced outer gaps. On either parity of the middle gap, the derivative of its exact scalar error has the sign of a quartic with sign pattern +,+,-,-, precisely one positive root, yielding at most four integer candidates. Evaluating its left-endpoint sign yields the sufficient strict concentration inequality. Exact rational independent matrix checks cover 3,168 finite schedules and the concrete witness; they do not substitute for the analytic quantifiers.

value.rationale: Finite-message interventions must allocate idle discussion time; heterogeneity makes pulse and averaging steps noncommutative, so optimization is not a standard commutative timing invariance. The general optimizer reduction yields a uniform four-candidate decision rule for arbitrarily many silent steps, and the proved nonempty concentration regime shows that a fourth broadcast can reverse the three-broadcast equal-spacing recommendation. This is an interpretable structural boundary in a minimal network rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical slice.
